fields.description: What this society calls this certification: First Aid, Psychosocial Support, Water and Sanitation. Display only; nothing in this app reads it to decide anything, and no course or certification name appears in any source file.
fields.label: Certification Type

fields.description: The stable business key, and the docname. A held certification points at its type by this key, so relabelling the type never rewrites history or breaks a report. This follows core's rule that configuration vocabularies are keyed by their stable business key while records about people and places get opaque IDs.
fields.label: Type Key

fields.description: An inactive type keeps the certifications already held under it but is no longer offered for new ones, so retiring a type does not invalidate anybody's training.
fields.label: Is Active

fields.description: What this certification covers and who needs it, in the society's own words.
fields.label: Description

fields.description: How long a certification of this type stays valid, in days, counted from the date it was completed. This is the whole of what drives expiry: a held certification's expiry_date is its completion_date plus this number, computed on save from configuration and never assumed to be a year. Zero means this type never expires, and a certification of a never-expiring type can never read as lapsed.
fields.label: Validity (Days)

fields.description: Whether a lapsed certification of this type makes its holder non-deployable. On by default, which is the ordinary rule: a volunteer whose first aid training has expired is not deployable on it. A society may switch it off for a type it treats as a record rather than a requirement. Read by volunteer/services/certification.py::deployability(), which derives the answer on every call and stores nothing.
fields.label: A Lapse Blocks Deployment
